code_path: src/pageindex_mcp/helpers.py :: classify_verdict() -> PASS gate at lines 1229-1236 -> strict `max_leaf_ratio < _pass_max_leaf` comparison with no hysteresis
suggested_fix: Implement hysteresis / tolerance-band / prior-verdict anchoring as prescribed by RFC-024's risk acknowledgment. Options: (1) Add a tolerance band (e.g., if prior verdict was PASS, use _pass_max_leaf + 0.10 as the threshold); (2) Store prior max_leaf_ratio in meta.json and only downgrade if the ratio exceeds threshold for N consecutive runs; (3) Use a smoothed/averaged max_leaf_ratio across runs. Widening the threshold further is NOT the right fix -- RFC-024 explicitly states this is the third consecutive widening and another widening must not be the approach.

symptom: "ﺣﻘﻮق اﻹﻧﺴﺎن - Copy.pdf" (UN human-rights training guide, doc_id 9bb72b96-77b1-4b7b-9053-6e51dfc6c7aa) regressed from a healthy Run-7 PASS (503,238 chars / 347 nodes / depth 5, verified from the Run-7 processed JSON: run7_processed_copy/9bb72b96-...json, whose root [Preamble] node text is only the two title lines "ﺣﻘـﻮﻕ / ﺍﻹﻧﺴـﺎﻥ" plus an <!-- image --> marker) to Run-8's reported FAIL of 382 total chars across the SAME 347-node/depth-5 tree. The hierarchy (headings/ToC/article titles) survived byte-for-byte while essentially all body prose vanished — the classic garble-gate patterns (RC1/RC2 CMap mojibake, RC3 garble-gate-hole) do not apply because there is no garbled text to detect: the content is simply absent from the tree, not corrupted.
root_cause:
This document's body text is not carried as ordinary Docling text nodes at all — the "Human-Rights" doc is explicitly cited in the RFC-005 tail-blob splitter's own docstring (helpers.py:1791, "Human-Rights=320k") as one whose paragraph text collapses into oversized picture/heading-only leaves, and its Run-8 preprocess.log entry shows an outlier child peak RSS of 9,573 MB (vs 1.5-5 GB for comparable docs, worker.py via preprocess_client.py:163-165) — consistent with many full-page 300-DPI picture crops being processed, i.e. Docling classified most/all pages as full-page Picture regions rather than exporting body paragraphs as markdown text.

The pipeline's own recovery path for exactly this scenario is `_recover_picture_text` in converters.py, but it discards the content instead of recovering it:

1. converters.py:1640-1653 — for any picture region whose bbox covers > `_PICTURE_PAGE_COVERAGE_THRESHOLD` (0.6, line 1349) of the page, the region is unconditionally skipped (`skip_reasons[i] = "page_coverage"`, line 1652) UNLESS `_COVERAGE_EXEMPT_NO_TEXT_LAYER and not _text_layer_has_content(page)` (line 1644) — i.e. unless the page has NO usable native text layer at all.
2. `_text_layer_has_content` (converters.py:1478-1495) is a PAGE-level, not region-level, check: `page.get_text("text")` over the WHOLE page, gated only by `len(text) > _PICTURE_OCR_MIN_CHARS` (20 chars, line 1348) and non-garbled. Any incidental native text anywhere on the page — a running header, footer, page number, or a caption sitting outside the picture's own bbox — trivially exceeds 20 chars and is non-garbled, so `_text_layer_has_content` returns True even when the actual body paragraphs are baked into the (skipped) full-page image and have no real text layer of their own.
3. Once the exemption fails to fire, the code `continue`s at line 1653 BEFORE reaching the clip_text capture logic (line 1658+), so the picture's OCR text and D1 clip_text capture (RFC-024) never run for that region — the page's entire body content is silently dropped, while heading/title text elements that Docling detected OUTSIDE the picture bbox (hence never subject to this gate) survive untouched. This produces exactly the observed signature: full heading/ToC structure intact, near-zero body chars.

A secondary reason nothing else catches this: `_document_level_text_fallback` (converters.py:1528-1580) only fires when `len(md.replace(_IMAGE_MARKER, "")) < _DOC_TEXT_FALLBACK_MIN_CHARS` (100 chars, line 1382). A 347-node heading/ToC-only tree easily produces well over 100 chars of title text alone, so the whole-document pdfium fallback never engages either — the 100-char threshold was calibrated for near-fully-blank markdown (0-char image-only docs like the SLA/MOU docs in this same corpus), not for a "structure survived, prose didn't" document.
code_path: src/pageindex_mcp/converters.py:1478-1495 (_text_layer_has_content), src/pageindex_mcp/converters.py:1630-1660 (_recover_picture_text page-coverage skip gate), src/pageindex_mcp/converters.py:1348-1361 (_PICTURE_OCR_MIN_CHARS, _PICTURE_PAGE_COVERAGE_THRESHOLD, _COVERAGE_EXEMPT_NO_TEXT_LAYER), src/pageindex_mcp/converters.py:1528-1580 (_document_level_text_fallback, _DOC_TEXT_FALLBACK_MIN_CHARS=100 at line 1382)
suggested_fix: Make the no-text-layer coverage exemption region-aware instead of page-aware: when a picture region covers >60% of the page, check for native text specifically OUTSIDE that region's bbox (page text minus the region's clip text) rather than `page.get_text("text")` over the whole page — a stray footer/page-number string outside the picture must not disable the exemption for content baked inside it. Concretely, add a region-scoped variant of `_text_layer_has_content` (e.g. subtract `page.get_text('text', clip=rect)` length from the page total, or compare the region's own `clip_text` length against `_PICTURE_OCR_MIN_CHARS` directly) and use it at converters.py:1644 in place of the current page-wide check. Additionally, make `_DOC_TEXT_FALLBACK_MIN_CHARS` scale with node/heading count or page count (or add a separate ratio-based trigger: markdown chars per Docling-detected page far below a prose floor) so heading-only trees like this one still route through the pdfium whole-document fallback as a safety net. Add a regression test fixture that mimics a full-page picture PDF with a thin non-representative header text layer, asserting the picture still gets OCR'd/captured.

symptom: مرسوم بقانون اتحادي رقم (13) لسنة 2022 (Federal Decree-Law 13/2022, Unemployment Insurance) regressed from a prior PASS (38 nodes, depth-3, 8.4k chars) to 2 flat nodes / 60 chars of unintelligible OCR garbage (",t t . 1 ·t r ; [• [ f"), stored as content_class=flat_prose, verdict=MARGINAL in meta.json (doc_id 724040b9-ae57-41a4-807c-4f4bdb459c65) — the audit correctly calls this a FAIL despite the stored MARGINAL verdict.
root_cause: Confirmed via direct re-conversion (docling CPU-forced + PyMuPDF) that the source PDF's page 1 has rotation=270 and its native text layer is CMap-corrupted mojibake for the entire document body (raw Docling markdown export = 2551 chars, almost all unreadable symbol soup, not Arabic) — same CMap-corruption class as sibling docs 9/19/cabinet_resolution_no_21 in this audit run. The pipeline correctly detects this as `reason="garbling"` on the first tree build and fires the Fix-3 `force_full_page_ocr` retry (client.py:955-1036, comment on line 962 literally names "مرسوم 13/2022" as the motivating case). Unlike sibling docs which crash to 0 nodes/0 chars, THIS doc's OCR retry completes mechanically but recovers almost nothing usable (the rotated page + 3 small logo-sized picture regions on it, bboxes ~90-145pt wide, are the only things the per-picture OCR/crop path in converters.py `_recover_picture_text` (lines 1583-1766) touches). Two of those three picture markers never resolve at all: converters.py lines 1760-1764 only set `result["decorative"]=True` (which lets `splice_figure_markers` strip the marker cleanly) when OCR yields nothing AND `crops[i]["rotation"] == 0`; for rotation!=0 (this doc's page 1 is 270) the comment says the rotation-correction path 'gets first crack' but no such follow-up recovery exists anywhere else in the codebase (the `rotation` key is read only at that one line) — so those markers survive as bare, content-less `{\"role\": \"image\"}` blocks (helpers.py:2161-2166, `_FLAT_RAW_IMAGE_RE` branch, comment: 'no matching PictureResult, so no index is set'). Because reason became `node_count<3`/`depth<2` (not `garbling`) after the retry, the doc is routed to the flat success path (client.py:1163-1169) rather than raising HR5's LowQualityTreeError. The flat-path garble gate (`_flat_text_is_garbled`, helpers.py:2061, called at client.py:1196) is supposed to catch exactly this case, but its two garble heuristics both have minimum-size gates that a 60-char residue falls under: `_is_garbled_blob`'s Latin-gibberish check (helpers.py:900-918) only fires when `len(latin_tokens) >= 5` (line 915), and `_has_sparse_mojibake` (helpers.py:940-952) hard-requires `len(text) >= 100` chars (line 949). The recovered OCR string is almost entirely single-character/punctuation fragments, so it never accumulates 5 real Latin tokens and is under 100 chars — both gates silently return 'not garbled', so `reason` never flips back to 'garbling', the VLM last-resort fallback (client.py:1206-1237) never fires, and 60 chars of garbage is persisted as a legitimate flat_prose document instead of being rejected or further escalated.

suggested_fix: 1) In `_is_garbled_blob`/`_has_sparse_mojibake`, treat "residual text too short to evaluate ratios AND originated from a garbling-escalation retry" as garbled-by-default rather than not-garbled-by-default — e.g., lower or remove the length/token-count floor specifically for text that already failed the initial tree-level garble check once (thread a flag through, or simply: any flat_md shorter than some floor, say 200 chars, on a document whose original tree build reason was 'garbling' should stay reason='garbling' rather than fall through as legitimately short content). 2) Give the rotation-gated decorative-flag branch in converters.py (lines 1760-1764) an actual second attempt (retry OCR/crop for rotation!=0 cases, e.g. re-crop with a rotation-corrected rect derived from the page's rotated dimensions) or simply set `decorative=True` regardless of rotation when OCR yields nothing, so these markers get stripped cleanly instead of surviving as unresolved bare image blocks — the current comment implies unfinished work, not intended behavior. 3) Verify the `_bbox_to_fitz_rect` region math is computed against `page.rect` taken BEFORE `page.set_rotation(0)` is applied at crop time (lines 1636-1693) — for rotation=270 pages the effective rect dimensions differ from the post-reset unrotated page, which may be silently mis-cropping the region and is a plausible reason the OCR yielded nothing on page 1 at all.

symptom: Run-8 audit reports "Reitlehrer - Schäden am Berittpferd.pdf" regressed from MARGINAL (4555 chars/10 nodes/depth-2) in Run-7 to FAIL (497 chars/8 flat nodes, doc_class 'unknown') in Run-8, attributing this to RFC-024-adjacent Docling non-determinism / heading-selection jitter.
root_cause:
The claimed Run-8 "497 chars / 8 flat nodes / FAIL" state for this document does not exist in the actual persisted store and cannot be reproduced from ground truth, so no code-level or Docling-non-determinism explanation is needed — the audit entry itself is the defect. Verified against MinIO (bucket `pageindex`, endpoint from .env MINIO_ENDPOINT=localhost:9000):

- Two uploads exist for this filename: job `81a4967d-30e5-444e-b882-38868efb46a3` (uploaded 2026-07-29T11:03:57Z, presumably the Run-7 source) and job `150adddf-6fd2-479d-930b-d4919556977f` (uploaded/processed 2026-07-30T12:22:18Z, the Run-8-era source).
- `processed/81a4967d-*.json` and `.meta.json` DO NOT EXIST in MinIO at all (list_objects with that prefix returns zero results) — so there is no ground-truth artifact backing the audit's cited "before" figures (4555 chars/10 nodes/depth-2) either; only the raw upload PDF survives for that job.
- `processed/150adddf-*.meta.json` shows `"verdict": "PASS"`, `"verdict_reason": ""`, `max_leaf_ratio: 0.2571` — not FAIL, and not doc_class 'unknown'.
- `processed/150adddf-*.json` (the actual current tree) contains 4 top-level titled sections ("[Preamble]", "2. Mitversichert ist", "3. Nicht versichert ist die Haftpflicht", "4. Schäden an Berittpferden (nicht Pensionspferden)") with real markdown table content (Docling table extraction intact), totaling **4082 chars across 10 nodes at depth-1** — closely matching (and effectively equal to) the audit's own cited Run-7 'before' baseline (4555 chars/10 nodes), not the claimed Run-8 'after' regression (497 chars/8 flat nodes/doc_class unknown).
- No Redis key for either job id survives (`redis-cli -n 1 keys "*150adddf*"` / `"*81a4967d*"` both empty) to explain a stale-cache-vs-persisted-store divergence, and no intermediate JSON/results file backing the audit's numbers exists anywhere in the repo outside the markdown report itself.
- Conclusion: the actual, only-available processed artifact for this document in the corpus store is healthy (PASS, real hierarchical structure, table content preserved) and contradicts the audit's per-document metrics. This matches the previously-confirmed failure mode logged in project memory (`fabricated-corpus-report-2026-07-17.md`, `corpus-audit-phase2-2026-07-17.md`): audit verdict tables/metrics generated without re-verifying against actual MinIO meta.json can be wrong. The `converters.py:2141-2153` gate-aware post_md/raw_md source-selection logic (`_recover_heading_depth`, `_has_recoverable_structure`) was inspected and is not implicated — its actual output for this document (150adddf) is the good 10-node/depth-1 tree, not the flat 8-node tree the audit describes. RFC-024's D0/D1/D2 changes are consequently not implicated either, since the regression they were framed as explaining is not present in the real data.

symptom: القرار التنظيمي لوزارة الاقتصاد1 (2) - Copy.pdf has NO meta.json in MinIO processed/ at all (verified via direct MinIO listing — 29 meta.json objects present, none matching this doc_name), unlike its 3 cluster siblings which each have a MARGINAL/node_count=0 meta.json. Reproducing the ingestion locally (uv run python -m pageindex_mcp.converters_cli on the doc_store copy) reproduces the exact preprocess.log failure: 'converter child exited 1' / '{"ok": false, "error": "LowQualityTreeError", "message": "low_quality_tree: node_garbling"}'.
root_cause:
This document's failure mode is NOT the pypdfium2 NULL-handle crash shared by the other 3 cluster docs, and D7 Tesseract-on-raster / D4 fitz / VLM recovery never get a chance to run for it — the cluster's shared-pattern hypothesis (RC1-pypdfium2-null-handle) does not actually apply here.

Full trace from a local re-run of `uv run python -m pageindex_mcp.converters_cli "doc_store/القرار التنظيمي لوزارة الاقتصاد1 (2) - Copy.pdf"`:
1. Docling successfully extracts a real (non-empty) text layer for this doc — no pypdfium2 NULL-handle exception is hit and `_document_level_text_fallback` (converters.py:1528) is never invoked, because Docling's own markdown already clears `_DOC_TEXT_FALLBACK_MIN_CHARS`. This is the key divergence from the other 3 scanned/image-only cluster docs, whose Docling markdown IS image-marker-dominant and DOES need (and fails) that fallback.
2. The LLM tree-builder runs to completion (~30 gpt-4.1/azure completion calls succeed) and produces a real tree structure.
3. `validate_tree()` (src/pageindex_mcp/helpers.py:1047) runs its checks in priority order: node_count OK, depth OK, bulk `_tree_is_garbled` (line 1057) does NOT trip (the garbled fraction is diluted below the bulk threshold across the whole flattened text). But the RFC-018 D3b per-node garble-ratio check (helpers.py:1059-1072) DOES trip: `_garble_check_nodes` (helpers.py:1002) uses the QF3 per-node script-inference override (helpers.py:1010-1026) — for nodes >=50 chars it infers the node's actual script and, when it disagrees with the filename-derived `expected_script`, logs "Script mismatch: filename-derived=%s, text-inferred=%s" (helpers.py:1018-1023) and uses the inferred script for garble-checking that node. For this doc the log shows exactly this 3 times: filename-derived=Arab, text-inferred=Latn — i.e. the CMap corruption decodes as Latin-script mojibake rather than Arabic, and `_is_garbled_blob` correctly flags these nodes as garbled against the Latin baseline. The garbled-node/total-node ratio exceeds `_GARBLE_NODE_RATIO_THRESHOLD`, so `validate_tree` returns (False, "node_garbling") (helpers.py:1072) — a DIFFERENT reason string than the bulk "garbling" reason (helpers.py:1058).
4. Back in client.py::index(), every recovery path that could have retried with OCR/Tesseract/VLM is gated on the literal string reason == "garbling": line 959 (_OCR_ESCALATION image-dominant escalation), line 1015 (VLM fallback), line 1048 (D7 Tesseract-raster garble recovery inside the VLM branch). None of these conditions match "node_garbling", so none of them fire for this document — the audit's open question ("verify whether the D4 fitz fallback + Tesseract actually fires") is answered: it does NOT fire, because the code path never reaches it.
5. reason also doesn't match the flat-doc-routing exemption (reason in ("node_count<3","depth<2"), client.py:1093/1169), so it falls straight through to LOW_QUALITY_TREES.labels(reason=reason).inc() and raise LowQualityTreeError(reason) at client.py:1405.
6. In production, converters_cli catches this, emits {"ok": false, "error": "LowQualityTreeError", ...} and exits 1; _run_converter_subprocess (worker.py:212) sees non-zero exit and raises ConverterChildError (worker.py:292) with error_class="LowQualityTreeError". Per Hard Rule 5 (validate_tree gates before save_doc), no meta.json/tree is ever persisted — which is exactly why this doc, unique among the 4 cluster members, has zero MinIO artifacts at all rather than a stored MARGINAL/FAIL verdict.

Net: this is the tree-quality gate (Hard Rule 5) working exactly as designed against a genuinely CMap-corrupted source PDF. The only real gap is a recovery-path coverage gap: "garbling" and "node_garbling" represent the same underlying failure class (garbled text, just measured at different granularities — bulk vs per-node), yet only "garbling" is wired to any of the three recovery attempts (OCR escalation, VLM fallback, D7 Tesseract-raster). A document whose garbling is concentrated in a minority of large nodes (tripping the per-node ratio gate before the bulk gate) currently gets zero recovery attempts and goes straight to LowQualityTreeError.
code_path: src/pageindex_mcp/helpers.py:1047 (validate_tree) -> helpers.py:1059-1072 (RFC-018 D3b per-node garble-ratio check, returns "node_garbling") -> src/pageindex_mcp/client.py:953 (first validate_tree call) -> client.py:959/1015/1048 (recovery gates, all require reason=="garbling", never match "node_garbling") -> client.py:1405 (raise LowQualityTreeError(reason)) -> src/pageindex_mcp/worker.py:212 (_run_converter_subprocess) -> worker.py:292 (raise ConverterChildError, error_class="LowQualityTreeError") -> no meta.json ever written (HR5)
suggested_fix: Extend the three recovery-path trigger conditions in client.py (lines 959, 1015, 1048) to also match reason == "node_garbling" in addition to "garbling" (e.g. reason in ("garbling", "node_garbling")), so documents whose garbling is concentrated in a minority of nodes (RFC-018 D3b gate) get the same OCR-escalation / VLM-fallback / D7 Tesseract-raster recovery attempts as documents that trip the bulk gate, before falling through to LowQualityTreeError. Verify with a targeted test using this document (or a synthetic fixture reproducing the Arab-filename/Latn-inferred-text mismatch) that the recovery path now fires and check whether Tesseract-on-raster output for this specific CMap-corrupt source is clean or itself garbled (if garbled, LowQualityTreeError should still correctly be the terminal outcome — HR5 must not be weakened, only given one more recovery attempt first).
